title: banks (LLM prompt templating) -- T1059 unsandboxed Jinja2 SSTI to RCE
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-44209 (GHSA-gphh-9q3h-jgpp),
a self-reported advisory for `banks`, a library for generating LLM
prompts with a template language.

Prior to 2.4.2, `banks` rendered prompt templates with a plain
`jinja2.Environment()` -- unsandboxed, permitting Jinja2's dunder-
attribute object-graph traversal. Any application that passes a
user-supplied string as the `template` argument to `Prompt()` is
vulnerable to Server-Side Template Injection. The advisory's own PoC:
`{{ self.__init__.__globals__.__builtins__.__import__('os').popen('id').read() }}`
passed to `Prompt(user_input)` then `.text()`, with a captured output of
`uid=1000(ak) gid=1000(ak) groups=1000(ak),27(sudo),...` demonstrating
full command execution. Templates loaded from a database, an external
API, or a user config file are all realistic vectors for reaching this
code path in a downstream application.

This corpus already carries `observed_ragflow_canvas_jinja2_ssti_t1059`
for a mechanistically identical bug class in a different product
(RAGFlow's citation-prompt generator); this rule targets the same
object-graph-traversal idiom, filed separately because the vulnerable
library, reachable code path, and affected downstream applications are
distinct.

Detection logic flags the same sandbox-escape idioms as the sibling
RAGFlow rule -- `__globals__`, `__builtins__`, `__import__`,
`__subclasses__`, `__mro__` -- appearing in content passed to a prompt-
template renderer, since these have no legitimate reason to appear in
ordinary prompt text.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (masci, via
GHSA and NVD; also tracked as RHSA via Red Hat/Bugzilla 2481713 for
distributions bundling `banks`), fixed in 2.4.2 (switches to
`jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment`).
